_what: PER-LINE DURATION SETTINGS THE WATCHDOG MUST PRESERVE WHEN IT REVIVES A DEAD LINE.
_why: R26-10 / RUN 27: watchdog_fenced.ps1's revive path built its ArgumentList from a LITERAL list
defaults -SpecsPerTask to 0 (= unset = the pre-2026-08-06 behaviour), so ANY line that died and
was revived SILENTLY REVERTED from 24 specs / h_rt 45:0:0 back to 8 specs / 15 h -- undoing the
duration lever mid-measurement, with nothing reporting that it had happened.
PowerShell binds a script at PROCESS START, so a supervisor keeps the argument vector it was
launched with. That is exactly why this has to be DATA read at revive time rather than a
constant compiled into a long-lived watchdog process.
_how_this_file_was_built: READ FIRST-HAND from the LIVE supervisor command lines at 2026-08-06T17:50Z via
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, never from a remembered value:
_core_is_absent_on_purpose: core (c1) carries the ENTIRE reported result and is DELIBERATELY still at 8 specs / 15 h.
Converting it is Tamer's call and only AFTER rung 30 banks (RUN 27 brief S5.5 item 2, S13).
Its absence here is load-bearing, not an omission: the reader in watchdog_fenced.ps1 ALSO
carries a hard guard that refuses to apply any override to 'core' even if this file gained one,
so the protection does not depend on this file staying correct.
_contract: A line NOT listed here is revived EXACTLY as before -- no extra flags, byte-identical behaviour.
A missing, unreadable or malformed file means NO overrides for ANY line, i.e. the fix fails SAFE
to the pre-fix behaviour rather than to a guess.
KEEP IN SYNC: if a line's specs/h_rt is changed by canary_duration.ps1 or a manual relaunch,
update this file in the SAME change, or the next revive will silently undo it.
